stem: A hospital is onboarding a travel nurse supplied by a staffing agency. Which verification plan best meets expectations for contract clinical staff?

options.A: Confirm current licensure or required certification, verify qualifications and competency for assigned responsibilities, and complete applicable hospital orientation
options.B: Confirm current licensure and rely on the staffing agency to determine competency and hospital-specific preparation
options.C: Verify prior employment experience and hospital orientation, but defer license verification because the nurse is employed by an external agency
options.D: Verify current licensure and certification only after the first independent shift so unit performance can be observed first

rationale: The Joint Commission states that Human Resources standards apply to contract staff who provide patient care. Its examples of compliance include primary-source confirmation of current license, certification, or registration; possession of the knowledge, experience, and competence appropriate for assigned responsibilities; meeting organizational education and experience requirements; and orientation to policies, procedures, key safety content, and specific job duties. Agency/traveling nurses are specifically included among examples of contract clinical services. Therefore A is the complete and best answer; the other options omit or improperly defer required elements.
educational_objective: For travel or agency nurses, verify required credentials and role-specific competency and provide applicable organizational orientation rather than assuming the staffing agency alone establishes readiness for the hospital assignment.
source_document_title: Contract Staff — Applicability of Human Resource Standards (HAP, CAH, AMB, OBS, NCC)
source_version_date: First published April 11, 2016; last updated January 8, 2026 (editorial changes only); accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Standards FAQ answer: all HR chapter standards apply to contract staff providing patient care; examples of compliance include knowledge/experience/competence appropriate to assigned responsibilities, primary-source confirmation of current license/certification/registration, organizational education/experience requirements, and orientation to policies/procedures, key safety content and specific job duties. Examples of contracted clinical services include agency/traveling staff (nurses, therapists, etc.).
source_claim_supported: Travel/agency nurses are contract clinical staff subject to applicable HR requirements, including credential verification, role-appropriate competence, and organizational orientation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care, p. 20, Assignment, Delegation and Supervision: assign/delegate to personnel with competency to perform tasks and evaluate staff ability considering allowable duties, competency, judgment and decision-making.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — travel nurse credentialing, competency, and assignment readiness
correction_summary: Converted the generic travel-nurse onboarding item into a precise contract-staff credential and competency verification item supported by the current Joint Commission FAQ. Replaced obviously irrelevant distractors with realistic partial-compliance errors and separated this construct from Q1295's orientation focus.
audit_findings: A contains each supported element relevant to assignment readiness. B improperly delegates the hospital's compliance responsibility to the staffing agency; C omits timely license verification; D delays verification until after independent care. The item does not claim that every travel nurse requires the same certifications; it says 'required certification,' avoiding unsupported universality. No second answer or cueing remains. Independent adversarial second pass passed.
